hints: Think about the units when you square the deviations from the mean.
Taking the square root returns the measure of spread back to the original units of measurement.

walkthrough.text:
State the relationship between units for variance and standard deviation:
$$\text{Units of Variance} = (\text{units})^2,\quad \text{Units of Standard Deviation} = \text{original units}$$

Explain the practical interpretability of standard deviation:
$$\text{Because } \sigma \text{ shares the same units as the mean } \bar{x},\text{ it allows direct comparisons of spread on the original scale.}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Contrast units:
$$\text{Variance has squared units, standard deviation has original units}$$

State why preferred:
$$\text{Standard deviation matches the scale of the mean}$$

ai_rubric.observable: State that variance is measured in squared units of the original data, whereas standard deviation is measured in the original units.
Explain that standard deviation is directly comparable to the mean and raw data because it shares the same linear scale and units.

hints: A standard deviation of zero means that no observation deviates from the mean.
Every notebook weighs exactly $240\text{ g}$. Compute $6 \times 240\text{ g}$.

walkthrough.text:
Interpret zero dispersion:
$$\sigma = 0 \implies x_i = \bar{x} = 240\text{ g for every observation } i = 1, 2, \dots, 6$$

Calculate the total mass:
$$\text{Total mass} = 6 \times 240 = 1440\text{ g}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
State meaning of zero spread:
$$\text{All 6 notebooks have identical mass of } 240\text{ g}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Explain that standard deviation = 0 means there is zero spread, so every single notebook has a mass exactly equal to the mean (240 g).

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the sample mean:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{\sum x}{n} = \frac{40}{5} = 8$$

Calculate the sample variance:
$$\text{Var}(x) = \frac{\sum x^2}{n} - (\bar{x})^2 = \frac{342}{5} - 8^2 = 68.4 - 64 = 4.4$$

hints: Evaluate $\sqrt{4.4} \approx 2.0976$ and round to 3 significant figures.
Standard deviation is defined as the square root of the entire variance expression, not individual terms.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the standard deviation:
$$\sigma = \sqrt{4.4} \approx 2.0976 = 2.10\text{ (3 s.f.)}$$

Explain the operational sequencing:
$$\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{\sum x^2}{n} - (\bar{x})^2} \ne \sqrt{\frac{\sum x^2}{n}} - \bar{x}$$
$$\text{The difference must be fully evaluated first before taking the square root.}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Explain order of operations:
$$\text{Variance must be fully computed before taking square root}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Explain that taking the square root prematurely (such as sqrt(sum(x^2)/n)) violates the order of operations because variance must be fully evaluated before square rooting.

hints: Remember that in $\sum f x^2$, the midpoint $x$ is squared, not the frequency $f$.

walkthrough.text:
Square the class midpoints:
$$x_1^2 = 5^2 = 25,\quad x_2^2 = 15^2 = 225$$

Multiply by frequencies and sum:
$$\sum f x^2 = 4(25) + 6(225) = 100 + 1350 = 1450$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Square midpoints and multiply by f:
$$4(25) + 6(225)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Set up products squaring the midpoints: 4 * (5^2) + 6 * (15^2).

hints: A standard deviation of zero means there is no price variation across the tickets.
Every ticket costs exactly $18\text{ dollars}$. Compute $4 \times 18\text{ dollars}$.

walkthrough.text:
Interpret standard deviation zero:
$$\sigma = 0\text{ dollars} \implies \text{Every ticket has identical price } = 18\text{ dollars}$$

Calculate the price for four tickets:
$$\text{Cost} = 4 \times 18 = 72\text{ dollars}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
State meaning of zero spread:
$$\text{Each ticket costs } 18\text{ dollars}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Explain that standard deviation of 0 dollars means all ticket prices are identical and equal to the mean of 18 dollars.
Calculate cost of four tickets = 4 * 18 = 72 dollars.

hints: Multiply each frequency by its midpoint and add: $2(5) + 5(15) + 3(25)$.
Divide by the total frequency $\sum f = 10$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate each product $f x$ and their sum:
$$\sum f x = 2(5) + 5(15) + 3(25) = 10 + 75 + 75 = 160$$

Divide by the sample size $\sum f = 10$:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{160}{10} = 16$$

ai_rubric.observable: Divide by 10 to obtain estimated mean = 160 / 10 = 16.

hints: Variance is $\frac{3050}{10} - 16^2 = 305 - 256 = 49$. Take the square root: $\sqrt{49} = 7$.

walkthrough.text:
Evaluate the variance and standard deviation:
$$\text{Var}(x) = \frac{3050}{10} - 16^2 = 305 - 256 = 49 \implies \sigma = \sqrt{49} = 7$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate variance = (3050 / 10) - 16^2 = 305 - 256 = 49, so standard deviation = sqrt(49) = 7.

hints: Divide by the number of students ($4$).

walkthrough.text:
Sum the test scores:
$$\sum x = 6 + 8 + 10 + 12 = 36$$

Divide by $n = 4$:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{36}{4} = 9$$

hints: Square each score: $36, 64, 100, 144$, and sum them to get $\sum x^2 = 344$.
Variance is $\frac{344}{4} - 9^2 = 86 - 81 = 5$, so standard deviation is $\sqrt{5} \approx 2.24$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the variance:
$$\text{Var}(x) = \frac{\sum x^2}{n} - (\bar{x})^2 = \frac{344}{4} - 9^2 = 86 - 81 = 5$$

Calculate the standard deviation:
$$\sigma = \sqrt{5} \approx 2.236 = 2.24\text{ (3 s.f.)}$$

hints: Divide $\sum f t$ by $20$ to obtain the estimated mean.

walkthrough.text:
Find the midpoints of each interval:
$$t_1 = 15,\quad t_2 = 25,\quad t_3 = 40,\quad t_4 = 60$$

Estimate the mean time:
$$\bar{t} = \frac{620}{20} = 31\text{ minutes}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate sum(ft) = 4(15) + 8(25) + 6(40) + 2(60) = 620, so estimated mean = 620 / 20 = 31 minutes.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the variance:
$$\text{Var}(t) = \frac{\sum f t^2}{\sum f} - (\bar{t})^2 = \frac{22700}{20} - 31^2 = 1135 - 961 = 174$$

Take the square root to find the standard deviation:
$$\sigma_t = \sqrt{174} \approx 13.1909 = 13.2\text{ minutes (3 s.f.)}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate estimated standard deviation = sqrt(174) = 13.19 = 13.2 minutes (3 s.f.).

walkthrough.text:
Subtract consecutive cumulative totals to extract class frequencies:
$$f_1 = 3,\quad f_2 = 9 - 3 = 6,\quad f_3 = 15 - 9 = 6,\quad f_4 = 20 - 15 = 5$$
$$\sum f = 20$$

Determine the class midpoints:
$$x_1 = 5,\quad x_2 = 15,\quad x_3 = 30,\quad x_4 = 55$$

Evaluate the variance:
$$\text{Var}(x) = \frac{21950}{20} - 28^2 = 1097.5 - 784 = 313.5$$

Calculate the standard deviation:
$$\sigma = \sqrt{313.5} \approx 17.7059 = 17.7\text{ (3 s.f.)}$$

Subtract consecutive cumulative totals to obtain class frequencies:
$$f_1 = 5,\quad f_2 = 14 - 5 = 9,\quad f_3 = 26 - 14 = 12,\quad f_4 = 30 - 26 = 4$$
$$\sum f = 30$$

Pair midpoints with frequencies and sum products:
$$\sum f x = 5(10) + 9(25) + 12(40) + 4(65) = 50 + 225 + 480 + 260 = 1015$$

Divide by 30 to estimate the mean:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{1015}{30} \approx 33.833 = 33.8\text{ minutes (3 s.f.)}$$

Evaluate the variance using the exact mean fraction $\frac{1015}{30}$:
$$\text{Var}(x) = \frac{42225}{30} - \left(\frac{1015}{30}\right)^2 = 1407.5 - 1144.6944... = 262.8055...$$

Take the square root to determine the estimated standard deviation:
$$\sigma = \sqrt{262.8055...} \approx 16.211 = 16.2\text{ minutes (3 s.f.)}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Calculate variance with exact mean fraction:
$$1407.5 - 1144.69 = 262.81$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate estimated standard deviation = sqrt(262.8055...) = 16.211... = 16.2 minutes (3 s.f.).

hints: Multiply each group count by its respective mean score: $12 \times 20$ and $8 \times 25$.
Divide by the combined student count $n = 12 + 8 = 20$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the sum of scores for each group:
$$\sum x_1 = 12 \times 20 = 240,\quad \sum x_2 = 8 \times 25 = 200$$
$$\sum x_{\text{comb}} = 240 + 200 = 440$$

Divide by the total number of students:
$$\bar{x}_{\text{comb}} = \frac{440}{20} = 22$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate totals: sum(x1) = 12 * 20 = 240 and sum(x2) = 8 * 25 = 200, giving combined sum 440.
Divide by 20 to obtain combined mean = 440 / 20 = 22.

walkthrough.text:
Sum both values to obtain the total sum of squares:
$$\sum x_{\text{comb}}^2 = 4908 + 5128 = 10036$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sum the sums of squares: sum(x_comb^2) = 4908 + 5128 = 10036.

hints: Take the square root of $17.8$ to find the combined standard deviation.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the combined variance:
$$\text{Var}_{\text{comb}} = \frac{\sum x_{\text{comb}}^2}{N} - (\bar{x}_{\text{comb}})^2 = \frac{10036}{20} - 22^2$$

Evaluate the difference:
$$\text{Var}_{\text{comb}} = 501.8 - 484 = 17.8$$

Calculate the combined standard deviation:
$$\sigma_{\text{comb}} = \sqrt{17.8} \approx 4.2190 = 4.22\text{ (3 s.f.)}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate combined standard deviation = sqrt(17.8) = 4.219... = 4.22 (3 s.f.).

hints: Let $y = x - 50$. The mean of $y$ is $\frac{15.0}{25} = 0.6$, so $\bar{x} = 50 + 0.6 = 50.6\text{ mm}$.
Variance is invariant to a shift: $\text{Var}(x) = \frac{\sum y^2}{n} - (\bar{y})^2 = \frac{41.25}{25} - 0.6^2$.
Take the square root: $\sqrt{1.29} \approx 1.14\text{ mm}$ (to 3 s.f.).

walkthrough.text:
Decode the mean using $y = x - 50$:
$$\bar{y} = \frac{15.0}{25} = 0.6\text{ mm} \implies \bar{x} = 50 + 0.6 = 50.6\text{ mm}$$

Compute the variance of the shafts:
$$\text{Var}(x) = \frac{\sum y^2}{n} - (\bar{y})^2 = \frac{41.25}{25} - 0.6^2 = 1.65 - 0.36 = 1.29\text{ mm}^2$$

Calculate the standard deviation:
$$\sigma_x = \sqrt{1.29} \approx 1.1357 = 1.14\text{ mm (3 s.f.)}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find coded mean and add 50:
$$\bar{x} = 50 + 0.6 = 50.6\text{ mm}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Let y = x - 50; calculate mean of y = 15.0 / 25 = 0.6 mm, so mean of x = 50 + 0.6 = 50.6 mm.
Calculate standard deviation = sqrt(1.29) = 1.1357... = 1.14 mm (3 s.f.).

hints: Find the sums of lengths: $25 \times 50.6 = 1265$ and $15 \times 50.2 = 753$.
Use $\sum x^2 = n(\sigma^2 + \bar{x}^2)$ for each machine.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the combined sum and mean:
$$\sum x_A = 25 \times 50.6 = 1265,\quad \sum x_B = 15 \times 50.2 = 753$$
$$\bar{x}_{\text{comb}} = \frac{1265 + 753}{40} = \frac{2018}{40} = 50.45\text{ mm}$$

Sum the two sums of squares:
$$\sum x_{\text{comb}}^2 = 64041.25 + 37810.2 = 101851.45$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find sum of squares for each machine:
$$\sum x_A^2 = 64041.25, \quad \sum x_B^2 = 37810.2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate totals: sum(xA) = 25 * 50.6 = 1265 and sum(xB) = 15 * 50.2 = 753, giving combined sum 2018.

hints: Recall that evaluating closeness to a target requires comparing the absolute deviation of each mean from $50.0\text{ mm}$.
Compare each machine's mean to $50.0\text{ mm}$: $|50.2 - 50.0| = 0.2$ vs $|50.6 - 50.0| = 0.6$.
Compare standard deviations: $0.80\text{ mm}$ vs $1.14\text{ mm}$ to assess consistency.
Explain that combining two groups with different means adds extra spread (between-group variation) to the pooled distribution.

walkthrough.text:
Compare target proximity:
$$|50.2 - 50.0| = 0.2\text{ mm} < 0.6\text{ mm} = |50.6 - 50.0| \implies \text{Machine } B \text{ is closer to target on average}$$

Compare process precision:
$$\sigma_B = 0.80\text{ mm} < 1.14\text{ mm} = \sigma_A \implies \text{Machine } B \text{ produces more consistent shaft lengths}$$

Explain the inflation of combined spread:
$$\text{Combined spread incorporates both the within-group variation and the between-group variation caused by } \bar{x}_A \ne \bar{x}_B.$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Compare mean to target:
$$50.2 \text{ is closer to 50.0 than } 50.6$$

Compare standard deviations:
$$0.80 < 1.14 \implies \text{Machine B has tighter consistency}$$

Explain combined spread:
$$\text{Separation between means increases overall spread}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Compare central tendency: Machine B is closer to the nominal target of 50.0 mm (mean 50.2 mm vs 50.6 mm).
Compare consistency: Machine B is more consistent because its standard deviation is smaller (0.80 mm < 1.14 mm).

Explain combined spread: the combined standard deviation increases because of both the higher internal variance of Machine A and the difference between the two group means (50.6 vs 50.2), which adds between-group variation.
